standard_prerequisites.name: Hamiltonian isotopies, the Calabi invariant and the group of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms with zero flux
standard_prerequisites.reference: the authors' own preliminaries at source lines 345-492
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement is phrased in the group of exact symplectomorphisms isotopic to the identity. The preliminaries are not re-proved; the quasi-autonomous generating Hamiltonian and the collar expansion of the theorem are the retained obligations.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Weinstein tubular neighbourhood theorem on the diagonal of a surface
standard_prerequisites.reference: the authors' own version at source lines 715-738, proved in full at source lines 740-810 and delivered here
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted proof invokes this lemma by its label. Its complete author proof is part of the retained material, so nothing is borrowed unproved.

standard_prerequisites.name: Moser's trick and the implicit function theorem on compact surfaces with boundary
standard_prerequisites.use: Only the standard C1-openness of the symplectic condition and the standard local inversion are assumed; every estimate that produces the C1-small quasi-autonomous Hamiltonian is retained.

core_obligations: Choose a primitive nu_0 of omega whose restriction to each collar A_C is (a_C - r^2/2) ds, by modifying an arbitrary primitive by the differential of a function that agrees with the correction on a reduced collar (source lines 695-700).

Build the Weinstein-type map: define kappa_0(r,s,R,S) = (R, s, R(S-s), (r^2-R^2)/2) on a neighbourhood of the diagonal in A x A, verify kappa_0^* lambda_std = nu_2 - nu_1 + d f with f(z_1,z_2) = -integral over [z_1,z_2] of nu_0 on the boundary, and extend it away from the boundary to obtain psi : U to V (source lines 740-810).

Define the generating function F on the cotangent bundle so that the graph of dF corresponds to the given exact symplectomorphism, and solve the equation that expresses phi in terms of F (source lines 811-959).

Produce the quasi-autonomous Hamiltonian H_t: show that the critical points of F give the extremal values of H_t over Sigma, use the collar form psi(r,s,R,S) = (R, s, R(S-s), (r^2-R^2)/2) to obtain the expansion H_t(r,s) = b_C + r^2 h_C(t,r,s) with |b_C| < epsilon and sup norm of h_C < epsilon, and conclude both estimates of the theorem (source lines 811-959).

proof_roadmap.step: Normalise the primitive in the collars and set up the arcs [z_1,z_2] and the Liouville form on the cotangent bundle.
Prove the Weinstein tubular neighbourhood lemma, including the explicit collar formula for psi and the boundary identity for f.
Use the generating function F of the exact symplectomorphism and analyse its critical points.
Read off the quasi-autonomy, the C1 estimates on H_t and phi_t, and the collar expansion b_C + r^2 h_C.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Theorem 2.8 at source lines 584-598, label t:quasi_autonomous: every exact symplectomorphism of a compact surface whose exact two-form satisfies the author's collar Assumption and which is sufficiently C1-close to the identity is generated by a Hamiltonian isotopy with a quasi-autonomous Hamiltonian, with C1-small H_t and phi_t and with the collar expansion H_t(r,s) = b_C + r^2 h_C(t,r,s) where |b_C| and the C0 norm of h_C are small. The retained proof is source section 2.3, which first has to build the tools it needs: it normalises a primitive in each collar to (a_C - r^2/2) ds, constructs the explicit map kappa_0(r,s,R,S) = (R, s, R(S-s), (r^2-R^2)/2) and proves a Weinstein tubular neighbourhood lemma for the diagonal of a surface with boundary, including the identity f(z_1,z_2) = -integral over the arc [z_1,z_2] of nu_0 on the boundary, and only then analyses the generating function on the cotangent bundle to produce the quasi-autonomous Hamiltonian and its boundary expansion. Neither the existence of a quasi-autonomous generator nor the boundary shape b_C + r^2 h_C follows from the usual C1-closeness theorem: the extremal points of H_t have to be produced from critical points of the generating function, and the collar expansion has to be read off from the explicit boundary formula for psi. The C1 estimates of items (i) and (ii) at source lines 589-597 are quantitative and are not restated anywhere else in the article.
